title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as companies pivot towards new technologies and partnerships. Funding rounds are closing, and the Pentagon is keen on integrating advanced capabilities, all while keeping an eye on the geopolitical chessboard.

themes.title: Funding Fuels New Ventures
themes.body: Skyroot's recent $60 million raise signals investor confidence ahead of its orbital launch, while True Anomaly's $190 million Series C highlights the growing appetite for space startups. With the Defense-Tech IPO window slightly ajar, expect more capital to flow into innovative aerospace solutions.

themes.title: Military's Tech Transformation
themes.body: The Pentagon's budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, underscoring a commitment to modernize capabilities amidst evolving threats. As AI and satellite technologies advance, the military's reliance on these tools is becoming increasingly evident.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions Rise
themes.body: Russian co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots raise alarms about space security, while GPS jamming in the Eastern Mediterranean returns to pre-2024 levels. The U.S.-Australian alliance is touted as a crucial countermeasure in securing space dominance.

themes.title: Industry Talent Shifts
themes.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears a critical design review, bolstered by a team of Blue Origin veterans at Starfighters. As companies seek experienced talent to navigate the complexities of space operations, the battle for skilled professionals is heating up.
